_comment: Cross-language contract for the per-user nav customization vocabulary (ADR-0139, ADR-0942 §6).
Before ADR-0942 the web derived its hideable set from band membership
(`VIEW_GROUPS.flatMap(g => g.views)`) and `apps/profiles/constants.py` asked in prose to
'keep the two lists in sync'. That derivation is what made the WORKSPACE band a trap: moving
`settings` into a band would have silently made it user-hideable, which the server rejects
with a 400 and which would have destroyed the ADR-0030/0139 guarantee that a user's nav can
So hideability is now an AUTHORED vocabulary on both sides, and this file is the third
artifact both sides assert against — a pytest for the server set and a vitest for the web
set. Drift therefore fails a pipeline in whichever language introduces it, instead of
`hideable` is the set a user may put in `UserProfile.hidden_views`.
`alwaysOn` is its complement: views that are band members but can never be hidden.
The two are disjoint and together cover every band member — asserted, not assumed.
Adding a hideable view: add the key here, to `HIDEABLE_VIEW_KEYS` in
`packages/api/src/trueppm_api/apps/profiles/constants.py`. Any one of the three alone fails.
